title: Pipe Method
definition: A method available on all Readable streams that automatically funnels its data into a Writable stream, automatically managing data flow and backpressure.
simpleExplanation: Piping is literally plumbing. If you have a hose shooting water (Readable Stream) and an empty pool (Writable Stream), the `.pipe()` method connects them. It automatically makes sure the hose doesn't shoot water faster than the pool can drain. If the pool gets full, `.pipe()` automatically pauses the hose.
realWorldExample: A user asks to download a massive video from your server. Instead of loading the video into RAM, you do: `fs.createReadStream('video.mp4').pipe(res)`. The file streams directly from the hard drive straight out to the user's internet connection flawlessly.
useCases: Connecting multiple Transform streams (like reading -> zipping -> encrypting -> writing)

answers.question: What does it do?
answers.answer: It attaches a Readable stream to a Writable stream, automatically passing data from one to the other.

answers.question: How does it handle backpressure?
answers.answer: If the Writable stream is too slow, its internal buffer fills up and it returns `false`. The `.pipe()` mechanism detects this and automatically calls `.pause()` on the Readable stream. Once the Writable stream drains, it emits a `'drain'` event, and `.pipe()` automatically calls `.resume()` on the Readable stream.
